query: Why does understanding your problem never fix it?
why_in_two_sentences: Both competitors agree with the thesis but stay at the level of assertion: Christian K Hughes frames it as insight versus capacity, and Practical Wellbeing retells the Buddha's poisoned-arrow parable. Ours supplies the mechanism (insight is content in language; behavior is produced by state, so the insight gets filed and overwritten within a day), the three gates, and insight-as-avoidance, with 34 FAQs written in the exact voice of someone this has happened to.
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Explains why an accurate insight wears off by the same evening: it arrives into body, attention, and language unchanged and gets filed against existing meanings
Lays out the three gates between a new thought and a changed life, with insight as only the first
Names understanding itself as a way of not changing, which neither competitor risks saying
Explains why you can see a friend's version clearly and go blank on your own, and why the pattern is hardest to interrupt in the room where it lives
34 verbatim FAQs including why therapy perfected the explanation but not the change, and why retreats fade by the second week

above_the_fold.ours: H1 is the query, the short answer gives the content-versus-state mechanism and the three gates, then recognition sentences; the call-with-a-friend scene lands immediately after.
above_the_fold.theirs: Christian K Hughes opens with the exact lived frustration (you can trace the pattern, and it still has not changed); genuinely good recognition, but the answer stays at insight-versus-capacity without a mechanism for what capacity is.

trust_signals: Both competitors are named individual practitioners writing on their own sites; ours names no one and cites nothing.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: none - both competitors hold the same thesis with less mechanism; ours is the deepest page on this query by a wide margin.
